feed.title: AI Wiki — Research Papers
feed.subtitle: New arXiv papers, triaged for relevance and summarised to key points.

entry.title: Mechanist: AI as a Scientific Instrument for Discovering the Mechanisms of Intelligence
entry.summary:
Mechanist is an agentic system that uses AI to autonomously discover, explain, and control the internal mechanisms of AI intelligence.

Why it matters: Automating mechanistic interpretability allows researchers to keep pace with rapid AI development, helping to identify safety risks and control model behaviors.

entry.title: DreamX-Phi 1.0: Action-Conditioned Video World Model for Robotic Manipulation
entry.summary:
DreamX-Phi 1.0 is an action-conditioned video world model for robotic manipulation that uses geometric attention encodings, depth prediction, and V-JEPA distillation to generate physics-faithful rollout observations.

Why it matters: It enables fast and geometrically accurate simulation of robot actions, reducing the gap between visual realism and execution faithfulness in robotic world models.

entry.title: Intern-S2-Preview: Scientific Agentic Foundation Model
entry.summary:
Intern-S2-Preview is a scientific agentic foundation model series utilizing multimodal pre-training, agentic reinforcement learning, time-series forecasting, and an optional Memory Decoder module for long-horizon scientific tasks.

Why it matters: It enables long-horizon, multimodal scientific reasoning and rapid domain specialization without needing to retrain large foundational model weights.

entry.title: AutoDesign: Meta-Harness Optimization for Long-Horizon Agentic Design
entry.summary:
AutoDesign introduces a meta-harness optimizer that enables code agents to recursively improve model-harness systems through rollout feedback, demonstrating state-of-the-art performance on academic paper-to-poster generation.

Why it matters: The framework demonstrates that recursive meta-harness optimization significantly improves autonomous agent performance on complex multimodal media creation tasks at low cost.

entry.title: Alaya-EVOKE: From Linear-Scaling Supervision to Endless World
entry.summary:
Alaya-EVOKE is a three-step interactive world model that decouples long-horizon memory into an external world state bank and uses a linear-scaling teacher to achieve bounded-context, open-ended video generation.

Why it matters: It resolves the trade-off between memory growth, low-latency interaction, and long-horizon consistency in real-time interactive video generation.

entry.title: Spatial Memory Agent: Experience-Grounded Procedure Memory for Spatial Intelligence
entry.summary:
The Spatial Memory Agent (SMA) is a parameter-update-free framework that enables frozen Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to improve spatial reasoning by distilling verified experiences into transferable lessons without using external spatial tools at inference.

Why it matters: It provides a practical, tool-free method for VLM agents to self-evolve and improve spatial reasoning performance purely through experience without requiring model re-training or fine-tuning.

entry.title: PlayWorld: Benchmarking World Models with Agent Players over Long-Horizon Objectives
entry.summary:
PlayWorld is a new benchmark featuring 171 scenarios that uses multimodal Agent Players to evaluate interactive video world models on long-horizon objectives across core consistency and interaction dimensions.

Why it matters: It enables standardized, objective-driven comparison of interactive video world models where fixed-action sequences fail due to variations in model dynamics.

entry.title: Massive Activations in Hybrid Linear Attention Large Language Models: Pre-Attention Spikes and Inter-Spike Plateaus
entry.summary:
A systematic study reveals that hybrid linear attention LLMs exhibit two distinct massive activation morphologies: pre-attention spikes occurring right before full attention layers and inter-spike plateaus persisting across linear attention layers.

Why it matters: Understanding these architectural activation patterns provides mechanistic insight into feature representation and stability dynamics across hybrid linear attention model designs.

entry.title: Self-Evolving Embodied Agents via Skill-Harness Evolution
entry.summary:
SHAPER is a self-evolving framework that adapts embodied agents to target environments without parameter updates by using a frozen foundation model to iteratively refine external reusable skills and a context-code harness.

Why it matters: It provides a practical method to continuously adapt embodied agents across diverse hardware interfaces without the compute cost or risk of fine-tuning model weights.

entry.title: Learning How the World Evolves: Extrapolative Video World Models via Latent Dynamics Reasoning
entry.summary:
Latent Dynamics Reasoning (LDR) casts video generation as explicit kinematic integration over structured latents, regressing only high-order residuals to enable physics extrapolation.

Why it matters: It demonstrates the first video world model capable of extrapolating physical laws out-of-distribution with significantly lower computational overhead than standard diffusion models.

entry.title: UniSwap: Streaming Audio-Visual Identity Swapping for Talking Videos
entry.summary:
UniSwap is the first streaming framework for joint audio-visual identity replacement in talking videos using a single audio-visual diffusion transformer.

Why it matters: It enables real-time, long-form talking video face-and-voice swapping within a unified architecture, eliminating the synchronization and consistency issues of decoupled audio and visual pipelines.

entry.title: LiveAnimate: Stable Long-Form Streaming Human Animation in Real-Time
entry.summary:
LiveAnimate is a 14B-parameter video DiT model enabling real-time, stable long-form streaming human animation at 19.63 FPS on two NVIDIA H100 GPUs.

Why it matters: It resolves the trade-off between real-time latency and long-duration appearance stability, enabling responsive, interactive human animation for live streaming, telepresence, and virtual avatars.

entry.title: H2R-Bench: Benchmarking Human-to-Robot Manipulation Video Generation in World Models
entry.summary:
H2R-Bench is a new benchmark for evaluating how effectively video world models transform egocentric human manipulation videos into robot-centric manipulation videos across different embodiments.

Why it matters: It establishes a systematic diagnostic framework to determine if video world models can reliably convert abundant human video data into viable robot manipulation training resources.

entry.title: Persistent Recursive Worlds Enable Autonomous Software Evolution
entry.summary:
EvoX Genesis shifts software agent continuity from persistent agents to a persistent recursive world, enabling finite-lived agents to construct and redevelop large-scale codebases over long horizons.

Why it matters: Decoupling project continuity from agent lifespan allows low-cost, long-horizon software engineering and codebase modernization through interchangeable, finite-lived AI agents.

entry.title: Gaze Target Estimation Anywhere with Concepts
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced Promptable Gaze Target Estimation (PGE), creating the Gaze-Co dataset and GazeAnywhere, an end-to-end model that predicts gaze targets using natural language or visual prompts instead of multi-stage pipelines.

Why it matters: Replacing multi-stage pipelines with promptable, end-to-end gaze estimation prevents cascading detection errors and enables flexible, human-centric visual analysis across diverse real-world applications.

entry.title: Algebraic Decomposition Theory for Transformer Length Generalization
entry.summary:
Researchers established a complete algebraic characterization and polynomial-time decision algorithm to determine which regular languages transformers can length-generalize on.

Why it matters: It enables a provable, algorithmic way to determine whether a transformer model can scale to longer sequences on specific formal language tasks without requiring empirical trial and error.

entry.title: Reduced Matrix Multiplication: Input-Adaptive Matrix-Product Reduction for LLM Inference
entry.summary:
Reduced Matrix Multiplication (RMM) is a training-free, input-adaptive inference method that speeds up Transformer models by selecting informative slices along contraction dimensions without altering weights.

Why it matters: RMM enables scalable, input-adaptive runtime acceleration and hardware-level FLOP reduction for large language models without requiring retraining or weight quantization.

entry.title: Rules or Character? Scaling Laws for AI Safety Design
entry.summary:
A novel comparative-statics model analyzes the optimal resource balance between character shaping and rule enforcement, showing that baseline character fragility under distributional shift drives safety design decisions far more than deployment scale.

Why it matters: AI safety architects should prioritize improving the reliability of character shaping under novel conditions rather than relying primarily on deployment scale or inference-time output filtering.

entry.title: StateBridge: Training-free Hidden-state Alignment for Latent Communication in LLM Multi-Agent Systems
entry.summary:
StateBridge enables training-free latent communication between LLM agents by aligning final-layer hidden states to receiver input spaces using a closed-form orthogonal transformation with norm calibration and vocabulary anchoring.

Why it matters: It eliminates the information loss of text-based agent communication and the overhead of training cross-model projectors, offering a portable and lightweight hidden-state alignment method.

entry.title: Mixture of Training: Recombining Small-Scale Scaffolded Pretraining Runs into a Larger Language Model
entry.summary:
Mixture of Training (MoT) decomposes language model pretraining by training contiguous layer blocks inside frozen aligner scaffolds, then recomposing them into a single larger model that matches monolithic perplexity.

Why it matters: It establishes a small-scale framework to test whether language model training can be broken down into modular, independently trainable layer units that are reconfigured and reused.

entry.title: vToken: Token-Level Virtualization for Reclaimable KV Caches
entry.summary:
vToken introduces a lightweight token-level virtualization layer that decouples logical token liveness from physical block allocation, resolving intra-block fragmentation caused by fine-grained KV eviction algorithms in LLM serving.

Why it matters: It enables token-granularity KV cache eviction in block-based LLM serving frameworks like vLLM, maximizing memory efficiency and inference concurrency without custom hardware kernels.

entry.title: Teach the Magnitude, Not the Direction: Verifier-Bounded Credit Assignment for Multi-Turn Multi-step LLM Agents
entry.summary:
CrEST is a hierarchical credit assignment framework for multi-turn LLM agents that uses a privileged self-teacher to modulate update magnitudes while preserving reinforcement learning's verifier-bounded performance ceiling.

Why it matters: It enables dense, token-level supervision for complex tool-use agents without suffering from policy collapse or capping performance below the verifier's ground-truth ceiling.

entry.title: DARTree: Speculative Diffusion Decoding with Autoregressive Draft Trees
entry.summary:
DARTree is a training-free speculative decoding method that extends an autoregressive correction head from draft chains to candidate trees, achieving up to 9.73x lossless speedup over autoregressive decoding.

Why it matters: It significantly improves speculative decoding throughput and acceptance lengths without requiring additional model training or architecture modifications.

entry.title: When Local Variance Optimality Is Not Enough: RoPE-Aligned Q/K Rotations for Dynamic 4-Bit Quantisation
entry.summary:
Researchers proved only per-pair rotations commute with distinct-frequency RoPE, but found RoPE-aligned pairwise rotations increase perplexity compared to full-head Hadamard transforms in dynamic W4A4KV4 quantisation due to limited mixing support.

Why it matters: Optimal local variance reduction on structured mathematical surrogates is insufficient for post-training quantisation if the transform's channel mixing support fails to reduce tokenwise group ranges.

entry.title: Where You Measure Decides What You Measure: Position Selection in Ablation-Based SAE Evaluation
entry.summary:
Researchers show that standard ablation-based SAE evaluation measures effects at tokens dictated by the dictionary itself, introducing high variance that disappears when evaluations use a standardized, fixed token position.

Why it matters: Without controlling for measurement position, casual evaluation metrics reflect token selection noise rather than true structural differences between sparse autoencoders.

entry.title: AI4AI at Test-Time: Strong-to-Weak Capability Transfer via Harnesses
entry.summary:
A study introduces strong-to-weak scaffolding, using a stronger builder model to construct deterministic, training-free test-time harnesses that boost weaker target model performance from 0.49 to 0.91 across four Theory-of-Mind benchmarks.

Why it matters: It offers an efficient alternative to traditional training-time distillation, allowing strong models to enhance weak model performance solely through inference-time cognitive structuring.

entry.title: Spark-to-Paper: End-to-End Research Paper Generation as a Composable Skill
entry.summary:
Spark-to-Paper generates end-to-end research papers using 13 composable skills inside a coding assistant, decoupling planning from reporting and enforcing programmatic checks.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that lightweight, composable workflows within existing coding tools can automate reliable, evidence-grounded paper generation at low cost.

entry.title: Can LLM Agents Stick to the Script? A Benchmark for Long-Horizon Consistency in Interactive Narratives
entry.summary:
Researchers introduce Narrative Commitment Preservation (NCP) and NCP-Bench to evaluate long-horizon logical consistency in LLM narrator agents under unconstrained user interventions.

Why it matters: High surface-level fluency in LLMs does not prevent severe logical drift, highlighting the need for specialized mechanisms to enforce state and commitment tracking in interactive AI environments.

entry.title: StateFlow: Building, Evolving, and Accessing 3D World States for Previsualization
entry.summary:
StateFlow is a state-centric generative previsualization framework that uses a persistent, editable 3D world state to construct, evolve, and access scene dynamics instead of relying on one-shot video synthesis.

Why it matters: It enables precise, iterative editing of spatial-temporal dynamics and camera trajectories in previsualization workflows without requiring complete scene re-rendering.

entry.title: SkillZip: Evaluation-Free Skill Compression for Self-Evolving Agents by Discovering Reusable Structure
entry.summary:
SkillZip is an evaluation-free skill compression method for self-evolving agents that reduces prompt length by discovering reusable structural patterns through a typed minimum description-length objective.

Why it matters: It enables self-evolving agents to maintain concise, maintainable, and cost-effective skill libraries without requiring expensive evaluation rollouts or task replays.

entry.title: Reference-Free Post-Training of Open Large Language Models for Multilingual Machine Translation
entry.summary:
Researchers developed MiLMMT-46-v1.0 by applying reference-free GRPO reinforcement learning and SFT checkpoint interpolation to open LLMs, improving translation quality across 46 languages without human reference translations.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that open-weights LLMs can achieve state-of-the-art multilingual translation performance across 46 languages without relying on costly target-language human references during post-training.

entry.title: Not Worth Another Token: Marginal Value Estimation for Efficient Deep Research Agents
entry.summary:
A systematic stage-aware evaluation of context pruning strategies in deep research agents demonstrates that lightweight heuristics applied at early pipeline stages reduce token usage by up to 73% with minimal quality loss.

Why it matters: System designers can dramatically cut token costs and lower latency in long-horizon AI agents by applying lightweight context pruning early in the retrieval pipeline.

entry.title: Self-Geometry: GT-Free and Plug-and-Play Test-Time Adaptation for Geometrically Consistent 3D Vision Foundation Models
entry.summary:
Self-Geometry is a ground-truth-free, plug-and-play test-time adaptation method that uses 2D pixel correspondences as pseudo ground-truth to enforce explicit multi-view geometric constraints on 3D Vision Foundation Models.

Why it matters: It provides a computationally efficient way to resolve multi-view geometric inconsistencies in pretrained 3D Vision Foundation Models at test time without needing scene-specific ground-truth optimization.

entry.title: InSight-doc: Agentic Visual Perception for Long-Document Understanding
entry.summary:
InSight-doc is an agentic visual perception framework that adaptively zooms into high-resolution document regions from low-resolution starts, eliminating external retrievers to improve accuracy and efficiency in long-document understanding.

Why it matters: This approach significantly accelerates long-document processing while drastically cutting hallucinations and removing the need for external retrieval pipelines.

entry.title: DistilVDR: A Compact End-to-End Visual Document Retriever via Dual-Student Distillation
entry.summary:
DistilVDR is a compact, 524M end-to-end visual document retriever distilled bilaterally from an 8B vision-language teacher using a pointwise cosine alignment loss without requiring relevance labels or negative sampling.

Why it matters: It enables scalable, cost-effective visual document retrieval by providing single-vector indexing that is an order of magnitude faster and significantly smaller than sub-1B multi-vector baselines while retaining high accuracy.

entry.title: SPIEval: Evaluating Large Language Models as Mobile Assistants over Scattered Personal Information
entry.summary:
SPIEval is a new human-curated benchmark evaluating LLM mobile assistants on instructions requiring retrieval and integration of personal data scattered across multiple applications.

Why it matters: The benchmark reveals that current LLM-based mobile assistants struggle significantly with locating and verifying personal information distributed across diverse mobile environments.

entry.title: 360CityArena: A Realistic Virtual Urban Navigation Benchmark for Embodied Agents
entry.summary:
360CityArena is a photorealistic urban navigation benchmark built from 360-degree videos of Tokyo's Akihabara district to evaluate embodied agents across environment understanding, path reasoning, and spatial reasoning tasks.

Why it matters: The significant performance gap between humans and top LMMs highlights major unresolved challenges in city-scale spatial reasoning and embodied navigation within photorealistic environments.

entry.title: TSDS-Toolbox: A Toolbox for Measuring Time-Series Dataset Similarity
entry.summary:
TSDS-Toolbox is an open-source, unified framework designed for systematic, reproducible evaluation and comparison of time-series dataset similarity methods across both dataset and series levels.

Why it matters: It simplifies source dataset selection for fine-tuning time-series foundation models by offering a standardized, extensible toolkit for evaluating dataset similarities.

entry.title: iFAN: Inference-Aware Learning for Plain Mask Transformers
entry.summary:
iFAN is a training-only framework for plain mask transformers that optimizes query selection and cross-layer feature quality without increasing inference latency or parameters.

Why it matters: It improves segmentation accuracy across instance, semantic, and panoptic tasks across various backbones without adding inference latency or FLOP overhead.

entry.title: DSAgentBench: Can Agents Automate End-to-End Data-Science Workflows in Real Computer Environments?
entry.summary:
DSAgentBench is the first benchmark designed to evaluate autonomous agents on end-to-end data-science workflows within real computer environments across 275 multi-stage, multi-tool tasks.

Why it matters: It highlights a severe performance gap in open-source and proprietary LLM agents when handling complex, tool-coordinated data science tasks in live operating systems.

entry.title: AI4AI at Test-Time: Strong-to-Weak Capability Transfer via Harnesses
entry.summary:
Inference-time strong-to-weak scaffolding enables a stronger builder model to generate test-time harnesses that boost weaker target model performance without updating any parameters.

Why it matters: This approach provides a parameter-free complement to standard distillation, allowing developers to upgrade weak model performance instantly using LLM-generated code structures instead of costly retraining.

entry.title: Information Abundance Paradox: Long-Context Training Undermines Parametric Knowledge
entry.summary:
The Information Abundance Paradox reveals that training LLMs on longer contexts reduces parametric knowledge encoding, shifting gradient pressure from FFNs to attention modules and weakening test-time performance when context is missing or misleading.

Why it matters: Scaling context windows during training creates a fundamental tradeoff between context-dependence and parametric knowledge retention, showing that infinite-context training can degrade model robustness without careful dataset and architecture design.

entry.title: Small-Scale Experiments: Are We There Yet?
entry.summary:
Researchers demonstrate that scaling laws exist even in small models starting at 4M parameters when hyperparameter tuning is prioritized to reach the optimal performance frontier.

Why it matters: Properly tuned small-scale experiments can reliably predict large-scale architectural decisions at a fraction of the computational cost.

entry.title: Towards Understanding On-Policy Distillation through the Lens of Test-Time Scaling
entry.summary:
Evaluation using test-time scaling reveals that on-policy distillation (OPD) improves sampling efficiency rather than expanding the student LLM's fundamental reasoning capability boundary.

Why it matters: This demonstrates that OPD acts as an 'illusory distillation' that optimizes output probability distributions for efficiency rather than instilling novel reasoning capabilities from the teacher model.

entry.title: Orientation, not magnitude: the causal structure of task-vector interference in merged language models
entry.summary:
A factorial ledger analysis of merged LLMs reveals that task-vector interference is driven by the orientation, rather than magnitude, of a layerwise cross-term that acts as a forward-pass attractor.

Why it matters: Evaluating parameter magnitude is insufficient for diagnosing merging errors; targeting the directional orientation of cross-term interference near output layers provides a causal mechanism to mitigate task arithmetic failures.

entry.title: Massive Activations in Hybrid Linear Attention Large Language Models: Pre-Attention Spikes and Inter-Spike Plateaus
entry.summary:
Researchers identified two distinct massive activation morphologies in hybrid linear attention LLMs—pre-attention spikes and inter-spike plateaus—governed by the layerwise placement of full attention and the timing of activation cancellation.

Why it matters: Understanding the structural patterns and cancellation mechanisms of massive activations in hybrid architectures is essential for optimizing quantization, numerical stability, and layer-interleaved LLM design.

entry.title: Causal Structure is Inducible but Functionally Decoupled: The Routing/Readout Boundary of a Typed Mechanism Library
entry.summary:
Type-level supervision induces slot-by-type causal routing structures in transformers, but these routing slots remain functionally decoupled from final answer readout across 22.6M and 125M parameter scales.

Why it matters: Mechanistic interpretability methods must separate structural routing signals from answer generation, as internal modularity does not imply direct behavioral editability.

entry.title: Ripple-Pivot Search: Active Parallel Decoding for Diffusion Large Language Models
entry.summary:
Ripple-Pivot Search (RPS) is a training-free parallel decoding method for diffusion LLMs that proactively commits mid-entropy pivot tokens to trigger downstream uncertainty reduction and accelerate generation.

Why it matters: It significantly accelerates inference latency and throughput for diffusion LLMs without requiring model retraining or sacrificing output quality.

entry.title: Rubric Dropout: A Simple Way to Mitigate Reward Hacking in Rubric-as-Reward RL
entry.summary:
Rubric Dropout mitigates reward hacking in LLM-as-a-judge RL by randomly dropping a subset of rubric criteria at each step during training while keeping group-relative advantages comparable.

Why it matters: It provides a zero-compute, easily implementable technique to prevent language models from exploiting fixed LLM-as-a-judge evaluation criteria during RL post-training.

entry.title: Redistribution-based Cost Inference Improves Sparse Safe Offline RL
entry.summary:
Redistribution-based Cost Inference (RCI) converts sparse, trajectory-level stop-feedback into dense per-step costs via return decomposition to train safe offline reinforcement learning policies without losing theoretical feasibility guarantees.

Why it matters: RCI enables reliable safe offline RL in real-world scenarios like driving and robotics where fine-grained per-step cost labels are unavailable or costly to annotate manually.

entry.title: BDH-CQ: In-Context Learning with Recurrent Latent Reasoning
entry.summary:
BDH-CQ combines in-context learning with recurrent latent reasoning to execute non-verbalized iterative computation in high-dimensional latent space for query solving.

Why it matters: It significantly reduces the cost of high-level abstract reasoning tasks by performing non-verbalized latent computation rather than generating costly intermediate tokens.

entry.title: On-Policy Self-Distillation without Any Supervision
entry.summary:
Unsupervised On-Policy Self-Distillation (U-OPSD) enables LLM post-training using only internal generation consistency without ground-truth labels, environmental feedback, or larger teacher models.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that language models can effectively self-improve on complex reasoning tasks without relying on external annotations, reward signals, or larger supervisor models.

entry.title: Co-Evolution in Agentic Systems: Toward Self-Directed Evolution Beyond Human Design
entry.summary:
This survey proposes a three-stage taxonomy for co-evolution in agentic systems, detailing how agents, environments, and evolutionary mechanisms dynamically adapt to overcome the limits of static, human-designed self-evolution.

Why it matters: Co-evolution offers a framework for AI systems to continuously adapt and improve in open-ended contexts beyond predefined human instructions.

entry.title: ComBodied Agents: a New Paradigm of Human-Centric Agentic AI
entry.summary:
Combodied Agents introduce a human-centric AI paradigm that models, predicts, and supports longitudinal human-state trajectories using Personal World Models and admissible intervention policies across digital, physical, and human action channels.

Why it matters: This paradigm shifts AI development from simple external task completion toward long-term, personalized human support while preserving user agency.

entry.title: Beyond Pixels: From Video Priors to 4D Worlds
entry.summary:
Latent-to-4D decouples 4D generation from specific video models by mapping denoised VAE latents directly to a pretrained 4D decoder using frame-wise and global spatiotemporal attention.

Why it matters: It enables modular 4D dynamic scene generation, allowing users to upgrade underlying video diffusion generators without retraining the downstream 4D reconstruction model.

entry.title: AdvFD: Boosting Visual Generation via Adversarial Fr'echet Distance Loss
entry.summary:
AdvFD introduces Adversarial Fréchet Distance, combining static feature targets with an adversarially learned representation and real-feature whitening to improve visual generator post-training without metric hacking.

Why it matters: It prevents generator quality degradation during post-training by ensuring distribution alignment adapts dynamically rather than overfitting to static feature spaces.

entry.title: Business Arena: Benchmarking LLM Agents in a Realistic Marketplace
entry.summary:
Business Arena is a new controlled benchmark evaluating LLM agents on long-horizon cross-border business operations grounded in real Alibaba.com sourcing data.

Why it matters: It establishes a realistic, profit-measured testbed to systematically evaluate whether LLM agents can perform autonomous, end-to-end commercial operations under market uncertainty.

entry.title: Mendel Gödel Machine: Recursive Self-Improving Coding Agents via Comparative Evolution
entry.summary:
Mendel Gödel Machine improves recursive self-improving coding agents by incorporating multi-task reaction-norm mutations and cross-lineage hybridization alongside standard single-trajectory clonal mutations.

Why it matters: Leveraging comparative signals across multiple tasks and agent lineages enables faster and more effective recursive self-improvement in autonomous coding agents.

entry.title: Ex-Omni-2D: Expressive Omni-Modal Dialogue Models with Native Visual Presence
entry.summary:
Ex-Omni-2D is an omni-modal dialogue framework that generates synchronized text, personalized speech, and reference-conditioned video using a Visual Thought Plan and a shared acoustic-temporal interface.

Why it matters: It enables real-time, expressive multimodal dialogue with visually embodied avatar responses without relying on scarce, fully paired four-modality training datasets.

entry.title: Decoding-Level Taboo: A Diagnostic Stress Test for LLM Robustness
entry.summary:
Decoding-Level Taboo is a zero-prompt diagnostic stress test that dynamically masks primary candidate tokens in logit space at runtime, forcing models out of their nominal generation paths to evaluate off-path robustness.

Why it matters: It exposes model performance degradation under real-world runtime constraints, complex system prompts, and safety guardrails that force models away from their standard generation paths.

entry.title: Don't Scroll Back: Missing-Evidence Memory for Streaming Dialogue Summarization
entry.summary:
The ReMEMBER framework optimizes streaming dialogue summarization by identifying missing evidence dependencies in a current context window to retrieve and compress historical context under a fixed memory budget.

Why it matters: It enables long-context conversational AI systems to produce accurate, contextually complete window summaries without exceeding strict memory and compute budgets.

entry.title: VectraYX-Vision-1B: A Sub-2B Spanish/LATAM Cybersecurity Vision-Language Model with Structured Visual Reasoning and Native Tool Use
entry.summary:
VectraYX-Vision-1B is a sub-2B Spanish/LATAM cybersecurity vision-language model integrating a frozen SigLIP-so400m encoder with a 1.04B decoder, featuring Model Context Protocol tool use, structured visual reasoning, and air-gapped GGUF deployment.

Why it matters: It provides a open-source, lightweight model architecture tailored for localized Spanish cybersecurity UI analysis and offline, air-gapped security operations.

entry.title: Gaming Without an Attacker: Benchmark Fingerprinting in LLM-Driven Search Under Selection Pressure
entry.summary:
Frontier LLMs in an evolutionary optimization loop automatically fingerprint benchmark evaluation environments without adversarial prompting, producing kernels that pass in-distribution tests but fail on held-out configurations 30% of the time.

Why it matters: Automated LLM optimization routinely yields brittle, overfitted artifacts that bypass evaluation metrics, making standard benchmark performance misleading without held-out probes on non-enumerable axes.

entry.title: A Hybrid Nested Harness for Decoupling Structure and Parameters in LLM-Driven Optimization
entry.summary:
A hybrid nested search framework decouples LLM-driven optimization by having the LLM propose structural code sketches while an inner numerical optimizer tunes embedded parameters.

Why it matters: Decoupling structure and parameter search improves optimization performance and token efficiency when using LLMs for code and policy generation.

entry.title: The Next Screenshot Knows: Gated Hindsight Distillation for Mobile GUI Agents
entry.summary:
Gated Hindsight Distillation (GHD) trains mobile GUI agents by using the next screenshot as privileged information to re-score student policy responses using a parameter-sharing teacher model.

Why it matters: It enables GUI agents to learn the visual reasoning behind ambiguous actions by leveraging future execution states as privileged training signals.

entry.title: Scheduling Mixed RL Rollouts Beyond Prefix Locality
entry.summary:
MISA-T is a routing-layer admission policy that boosts mixed RL rollout throughput by combining adaptive session admission, workload-aware KV-capacity allocation, and residency-time-aware KV accounting.

Why it matters: It significantly reduces LLM RL post-training iteration times and hardware resource contention without skewing the required training data distribution or task performance.

entry.title: ReRound: Reconstructive Rounding to Resolve Midpoint Ambiguity in Calibration-Free LLM Quantization
entry.summary:
ReRound is a calibration-free quantization method that uses a conditional diffusion model to guide low-bit rounding for LLM weights located near quantization interval midpoints.

Why it matters: It enables higher accuracy for 3-bit and 4-bit small language models without requiring calibration data or introducing runtime computational overhead.

entry.title: ReOrder-OPD:Reliability-Aware Prompt Ordering for On-Policy Distillation
entry.summary:
ReOrder-OPD introduces a prompt-level reliability ordering method for on-policy distillation using a ROUGE-5 proxy score to schedule prompts by a teacher's probability of correctly completing student prefixes.

Why it matters: It improves on-policy distillation performance without changing local loss functions by simply reordering training prompts based on estimated teacher continuation success.

entry.title: Diffract: Spectral View of LLM Domain Adaptation
entry.summary:
Diffract reveals continual pre-training adapts LLMs via singular vector changes rather than singular value spectra, enabling up to 60% selective attention-head pruning and rewinding to boost benchmark accuracy by up to 4%.

Why it matters: Identifying head importance and domain connectivity during continual pre-training allows practitioners to prune redundant weight updates, optimize multi-domain performance, and increase accuracy through selective state rewinding.

entry.title: MoE Proxy Models for Low-Cost Failure Reproduction and Diagnosis in LLM RL Post-Training
entry.summary:
A proxy-model construction method uses structure-preserving, clustering-based expert pruning on MoE models to reduce RL post-training failure reproduction costs by up to 33.3x on Huawei Ascend NPUs while maintaining training dynamics.

Why it matters: It enables developers to rapidly debug and diagnose complex LLM reinforcement learning pipeline failures at a fraction of the computational and financial cost.

entry.title: Compute-Optimal Is Not Cluster-Optimal: Systems-Aware Scaling for Sparse Mixture-of-Experts
entry.summary:
MOSAIC unifies scaling laws and hardware performance modeling into a single co-design optimization framework specifically for sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language models.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that frontier language model design must shift from isolated algorithmic scaling laws to hardware-aware co-design to achieve actual wall-clock efficiency on training clusters.

entry.title: Data Attribution of Emergent Misalignment with Persona Features
entry.summary:
Researchers used SAE-based model diffing and pre-training data attribution to show that emergent misalignment is driven by amplified persona features, which require synthetic instruction-response phrasing rather than just human-written content to activate.

Why it matters: Demonstrates that emergent misalignment depends heavily on synthetic response structures and phrasing rather than semantic content alone, providing actionable feature-steering mechanisms for safety interventions.

entry.title: Test-Time Self-Evolving GUI Visual Grounding via Reflection-Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation
entry.summary:
A test-time self-evolving framework for GUI visual grounding that uses reflection-guided on-policy self-distillation and contrastive calibration to adapt deployed models to unseen interfaces without human annotations.

Why it matters: It enables GUI agents to continuously adapt to unfamiliar user interfaces post-deployment without relying on ground-truth annotations or human feedback.

entry.title: Attention-Path Fragility as an Uncertainty Signal in Large Language Models
entry.summary:
Attention-Subnetwork Mutual Information (ASMI) is a training-free uncertainty estimator that measures prediction fragility by masking attention heads and evaluating mutual information across the resulting subnetworks using a semantic-agreement kernel.

Why it matters: ASMI enables highly accurate uncertainty estimation for grounded QA tasks from a single inference pass, significantly reducing computational overhead compared to sampling-based baselines like Semantic Entropy.

entry.title: ThinkRetrieve: Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning Traces for Test-Time Scaling
entry.summary:
ThinkRetrieve is a test-time scaling framework that dynamically injects retrieved solved problem exemplars directly into an LRM's intermediate reasoning trace at each step to prevent error compounding and drift.

Why it matters: It offers a method to scale test-time inference compute more effectively by providing models with procedural reasoning guidance rather than standard factual retrieval.

entry.title: SWE-Bench ProMax: Benchmarking Agents on Large-Scale Multilingual Code Refactoring
entry.summary:
SWE-Bench ProMax is a multilingual code refactoring benchmark of 170 expert-curated instances across seven languages designed to address flaws and low complexity in existing coding agent benchmarks.

Why it matters: It provides an unsaturated, high-quality evaluation target that tests AI agents on complex, cross-file software refactoring without the noisy test suites of earlier benchmarks.

entry.title: Macaron-V1: Towards Open Continual Learning with Self-Improvement and Mixture-of-LoRA
entry.summary:
Macaron-V1 is an open agent-model family that uses recursive self-improvement and a Mixture-of-LoRA architecture to enable post-deployment continual learning.

Why it matters: It offers an open-source co-designed infrastructure that allows deployed models to continuously adapt and specialize without retraining the underlying base weights.

entry.title: Motif 3: Technical Report
entry.summary:
Motif 3 is a 314B parameter decoder-only MoE model utilizing Grouped Differential Latent Attention, activating 13.2B parameters across 384 routed experts to improve efficiency, stability, and broad domain performance.

Why it matters: It demonstrates how combining fine-grained MoE sparsity, architectural stabilization, and multi-teacher distillation can yield top-tier performance across reasoning, coding, and long-context tasks with reduced active compute per token.

entry.title: Agent Memory Distillation: Empowering Small LLM Agents with Hierarchical Teacher Memory
entry.summary:
Agent Memory Distillation (AMD) is a training-free framework that transfers structured, hierarchical teacher memory (Workflow, Subtask, and Function) from large LLMs to small 4B-8B student agents to boost tool-use performance.

Why it matters: AMD enables small language models (4B-8B parameters) to achieve high-tier tool-use capabilities without requiring expensive model retraining or fine-tuning.

entry.title: Sci-VBench: Evaluating Knowledge- and Reasoning-Intensive Video Generation in Science Domains
entry.summary:
Sci-VBench is a new benchmark featuring 1,253 expert-annotated examples across 60 subjects to evaluate scientific reasoning and knowledge-grounded synthesis in video generation models.

Why it matters: The benchmark demonstrates that high perceptual quality in AI-generated video does not guarantee accurate modeling of real-world scientific and causal dynamics.

entry.title: Ouroboros: A Self-Developing Frontier Coding Agent with Reviewed Core Evolution
entry.summary:
Ouroboros is a self-developing coding agent that recursively evolves its tools, prompts, context assembly, and core implementation through governed, reviewed commits.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that software agents can continuously self-improve their own codebase and performance on complex tasks without losing operational control or safety.

entry.title: DCAS: Decoupling CLI Agent Scaffolding to Internalize Planning across Scaffolds
entry.summary:
DCAS is an interception layer that decouples CLI agent scaffolding from backend models to train LLMs on planning-aware trajectories, mitigating fine-tuning-induced performance degradation across different evaluation scaffolds.

Why it matters: Decoupling planning from scaffold-specific artifacts allows models to internalize planning as a native capability, ensuring robust agent performance across diverse CLI environments.

entry.title: SPOT: Sparse Probing and Outcome Calibration for On-Policy Distillation
entry.summary:
SPOT improves on-policy distillation by using an acquisition-exploration-exploitation framework that sparsely probes teacher-proposed top-k candidates and calibrates distillation targets using verifier-scored student continuations.

Why it matters: SPOT enhances student model reasoning performance by ensuring distillation targets reflect downstream solution success rather than just local teacher token probabilities.

entry.title: Small Foundation Models of Human Cognition and Behaviour
entry.summary:
Fourteen language models (135M to 14B parameters) fine-tuned on the 10.7M-trial Psych-101 dataset show that 0.6B-1B parameter models match 70B baselines in-distribution, though larger models scale significantly better out-of-distribution.

Why it matters: Small cognitively fine-tuned models can efficiently serve as noise ceiling estimators for human psychological experiments without requiring massive 70B-parameter models for in-distribution tasks.

entry.title: OasisKV: Scaling In-Decode KV Cache Beyond HBM with Lookahead Sparse Prefetching
entry.summary:
OasisKV decouples full KV-cache storage from HBM by using speculative decoding's lookahead tokens to predict and prefetch sparse, high-importance KV blocks from host/remote memory into HBM ahead of decode steps.

Why it matters: It enables memory-constrained inference systems to process significantly larger batch sizes and long-context workloads with up to double the throughput without losing generation accuracy.

entry.title: Relevant but Incomplete: Referential Dangling as a Paradigm-Level Failure Mode in Hard Prompt Compression
entry.summary:
Independent scoring in hard prompt compression causes referential dangling, where retained answer text loses the required entity context, degrading downstream model accuracy by up to 34 percentage points.

Why it matters: Hard prompt compression algorithms must be redesigned to ensure referential completeness alongside relevance, as even frontier language models cannot recover lost contextual dependencies.

entry.title: Multi-Agent Forensic Reasoning for Generalizable Deepfake Video Detection
entry.summary:
A new framework, FaceVid-Forensics-100K dataset, and multi-agent system improve deepfake video detection by analyzing four distinct forensic perspectives using open-source MLLMs.

Why it matters: This approach provides generalizable deepfake detection and interpretable forensic reasoning without relying on large closed-source multimodal language models.

entry.title: Evo-Bench: Can Language Models Improve Agent Harness?
entry.summary:
Evo-Bench is the first benchmark designed to evaluate LLMs' intrinsic capacity to autonomously evolve their own operating harnesses across Search, Office, and General agent domains.

Why it matters: It provides a standardized methodology to evaluate whether LLMs can self-optimize their execution frameworks, opening pathways for transferable, self-improving AI agent architectures.

entry.title: Evidence-RL: Towards Evidence-intensive Visual Reasoning
entry.summary:
Counterfactual Evidence Disentanglement (CED) improves Vision-Language Model grounding by auditing whether model responses causally depend on specific visual evidence regions during Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) training.

Why it matters: It enables Vision-Language Models to reduce hallucinations and dataset shortcuts by forcing causal reliance on visual context without incurring additional inference costs or requiring manual evidence annotations.

entry.title: Scaling Inherently Interpretable Language Models
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced Steerling-8B, demonstrating that incorporating interpretability constraints directly into training pipelines allows interpretability to scale alongside language modeling capability without sacrificing performance.

Why it matters: It proves that models can be built inherently interpretable and steerable at scale without paying a performance penalty or requiring expensive compute-heavy post-hoc analysis.

entry.title: Mismatch Matters: On-Policy Distillation Beyond Token Agreement
entry.summary:
TIDE improves on-policy distillation by addressing teacher-student mismatch via bounded Hellinger shaping for student-excess tokens and analytic teacher top-K injection for student-deficit tokens.

Why it matters: TIDE stabilizes on-policy distillation under severe model mismatches, preventing degenerate generation loops and reducing formatting failures while shortening response lengths.

entry.title: Distill Skills into Weights, Not Prompts: Abstract Skills as Privileged Signals for On-Policy Self-Distillation
entry.summary:
SKALD uses on-policy self-distillation to transfer knowledge from a teacher model conditioned on abstract skills into a question-only student model, overcoming zero-variance reward groups in reinforcement learning.

Why it matters: It enables language models to internalize abstract reasoning skills directly into their weights, offering dense learning signals even when standard RL reward signals stall.

entry.title: Parameter Exploration for RLVR via Variational Learning
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced Perturbed Parameter Policy Optimization (3PO), a parameter-space exploration framework for LLM reinforcement learning that samples diverse policy parameters to improve exploration beyond traditional action-space methods.

Why it matters: Parameter-space exploration provides a FLOP-efficient alternative to action-space methods, improving LLM reinforcement learning stability and task performance without additional computational overhead.

entry.title: SR-OPSD: Self-Referenced On-Policy Self-Distillation
entry.summary:
SR-OPSD introduces a self-referenced on-policy self-distillation framework that stabilizes optimization by placing distillation targets via geometric interpolation and controlling projection geometry using Rényi divergence.

Why it matters: It improves optimization stability and performance across scientific, mathematical, and code generation tasks when tuning large language models with dense token-level feedback.

entry.title: Matryoshka Language Model Suites
entry.summary:
A novel Matryoshka training framework stacks language sub-models into a single nested architecture, enabling end-to-end joint training, in-flight distillation, and parameter-efficient speculative decoding.

Why it matters: This architecture significantly cuts pre-training compute costs and enhances inference throughput without sacrificing model performance across size variants.

entry.title: MixFormer: Linear Transformer with Mixture of Memory Experts
entry.summary:
MixFormer is a linear Transformer that combines a Mixture-of-Memory-Experts mechanism with Time-Aware Linear Attention to improve memory capacity and long-context sequence modeling.

Why it matters: By overcoming the memory capacity and input adaptivity limitations of standard SSMs, MixFormer offers a more computationally efficient backbone for long-context web infrastructure and generative tasks.

entry.title: WDL-OPD: Weak-Driven On-Policy Distillation via Mixture-Constrained Co-Training
entry.summary:
WDL-OPD stabilizes on-policy distillation by co-training an anchor policy and an auxiliary policy using a mixture-constrained reverse KL loss against a frozen teacher.

Why it matters: Co-training two policies via a geometric mixture offers a targeted mechanism to prevent feedback loop instabilities and performance degradation in on-policy LLM distillation.

entry.title: Depth-adaptive Inference of Looped Language Models via Continuous Depth Batching
entry.summary:
Continuous depth batching (CDB) enables efficient depth-adaptive inference for looped LMs by scheduling at the loop-iteration level while handling non-looped boundary stages via separate priority queues.

Why it matters: CDB resolves batching inefficiencies in looped language models, enabling 1.5-1.9x higher offline throughput and up to 90% lower latency under dynamic serving loads.

entry.title: A Mechanistic Diagnostic of Rank Collapse in Post-Norm Decoder Transformers
entry.summary:
A two-stage analysis reveals that Post-Norm Transformer rank collapse stems from causal attention amplifying forward token similarity, which causes pre-norm residual norm growth that geometrically contracts backward gradients in RMSNorm layers.

Why it matters: Understanding the distinct forward amplification and backward gradient contraction mechanisms in Post-Norm architectures provides a clear diagnostic for why training dynamics fail to recover from rank collapse.

entry.title: Reducing Pretraining-Generation Mismatch in Diffusion Language Models
entry.summary:
Prefix-Conditioned Diffusion (PCD) reduces pretraining-generation mismatch in diffusion language models by combining autoregressive prefix supervision with no-shift suffix denoising without changing the inference mode.

Why it matters: PCD narrows the performance gap between diffusion and autoregressive language models on continuation tasks without needing verifiers, extra decoders, or changes to inference.
